summary: Albert Graeter was an Indologist and linguist. He served as a missionary with the Basel Mission (circa 1859-1877) and taught English at the University of Basel (1870-1908).

Albert Grünwedel worked in Indology, Tibetology, and history/archaeology. After earning his Dr. phil. at the University of Munich (1876-1883), he served at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin from 1881, directing its Indische Abteilung from 1904 to 1921.
Albert Henry Allen was an Indologist who earned an A.B. from the University of California, Los Angeles in 1898 and an M.A. from Harvard University in 1900.

Albert Henry Arden was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from Christ's College, Cambridge (circa 1858-1861) and served as University Lecturer in Telugu and Tamil at the University of Cambridge from 1882 to 1890.

Albert Henry Longhurst worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under John Marshall and served as Superintendent of the Southern Circle for the Archaeological Survey of India (1910-1911).

Albert Hoefer worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Greifswald, Göttingen, Berlin, and Königsberg under scholars including Bopp, Grimm, and Lachmann. He taught at Humboldt University of Berlin and served as professor at the University of Greifswald from 1840 to 1883.
Albert Hofmann studied at the University of Zurich (circa 1925-1929) and subsequently held a post at Novartis from circa 1929 to 1971.

Albert Ippel was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Freiburg, Berlin, and Bonn (Ph.D.). He held posts at the University of Breslau (circa 1923-1940), Humboldt University of Berlin (1940), and the University of Hamburg (1947-1954).
Albert Johannes de Jong was an Indologist. He studied at Utrecht University, where he completed his PhD in 1917 under the supervision of Willem Caland.

Albert Joris van Windekens was a linguist, Iranian, and Indology scholar. He earned his doctorate at KU Leuven under Albert Joseph Carnoy and Jean Filliozat, and later directed the Centre international de dialectologie générale (circa 1970-1989).

Albert Joseph Carnoy was a linguistics and Iranian studies scholar. He completed his dissertation at KU Leuven, where he served as a professor from 1904 to 1955, and held posts at Columbia University and UC Berkeley.

Albert Lutz is a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at the University of Zurich under Eberhard Fischer and served as curator of Chinese art (1982) and director (1998-2019) at Museum Rietberg.

Albert Schweitzer worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied under Wilhelm Deecke and at Strasbourg, Tübingen, and the German University of Prague, later holding a post at the University of Strasbourg from circa 1902 to 1913.
Albert Sechehaye was a linguist who studied at the University of Geneva (circa 1889-1893) under Ferdinand de Saussure. He later held a post at the University of Geneva from circa 1903 to 1946.

Albert Socin worked in linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies. After studying at the University of Basel (circa 1862-1866), he held academic posts at Basel (circa 1871-1876), Tübingen (circa 1876-1890), and Leipzig (circa 1890-1899).

Albert Ten Eyck Olmstead was an archaeologist and historian who earned his Ph.D. at Cornell. He held posts at the University of Missouri, University of Chicago (1917-1929), and the Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures (from 1929).

Albert Thumb was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Freiburg, Leipzig, and Heidelberg under Brugmann, Osthoff, and Thurneysen, and held professorships at the Universities of Freiburg, Marburg (1901), and Strasbourg (1909).

Albert Welter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara, served at the University of Winnipeg (circa 1995-2014), and joined the University of Arizona in 2013 as department head.

Albert von Le Coq was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Seminar for Oriental Languages and worked at the Ethnological Museum of Berlin, becoming Director of the Asian Department in 1914.
Alberto Todeschini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2010) and has held a guest post at Kyoto University.
